tool_args.old_string: All experiments use MuJoCo simulation (SafeLIBERO, two VLA families, four pick-and-place tasks); action collapse is structurally general but untested on other benchmarks and real hardware. The EE-only SDF null result is specific to auxiliary loss integration and should not be extrapolated to alternative pathways (Section~\ref{sec:related}). The sim-to-real gap introduces uncertainty---collision detection and contact dynamics differ on physical hardware---though the core diagnostic (near-zero motor output inflating CAR) is kinematic, and dfCAR requires only EE position logging. Statistical power is limited by $n{=}3$ seeds per condition (MDE ${\approx}$ 5.6\,pp at 80\% power); effects in the 2--5\,pp range cannot be resolved at this scale. Oracle experiments used largely action-collapsed baselines; validation on actively moving policies and full-body SDF remain necessary before generalizing the counterproductive finding. Run-to-run variance is approximately 0.5\,pp CAR and 5.5\,pp TSR, bounding measurement precision. We emphasize that our conclusion is absence of a detectable benefit at our experimental scale; a genuine 2--5\,pp effect remains consistent with our data but would require substantially larger experiments to resolve.
tool_args.new_string: All experiments use MuJoCo simulation (SafeLIBERO, two VLA families, four pick-and-place tasks); action collapse is structurally general but untested on other benchmarks and real hardware. The EE-only SDF null result is specific to auxiliary loss integration and should not be extrapolated to alternative pathways such as constrained optimization or runtime filtering (Section~\ref{sec:related}).
